title: Interrogativa
subtitle: Quis, quid, cur, ubi — verba interrogativa, et -ne/num/nonne.
objectives: Uti adverbiis interrogativis frequentibus (cur, ubi, quando, quomodo, quot)

content.intro: 'Quis venit?' rogat Iulia. 'Ego,' dicit Marcus, ridens. 'Cur tam laetus es?' 'Habeone causam dicere?' 'Nonne mihi omnia narras semper?' 'Num putas me tacere posse?' Quis, cur, nonne, num — verba et particulae interrogativa.
content.explanation:
“Quis venit?” rogat Iūlia. “Ego,” dīcit Mārcus, rīdēns. “Cūr tam laetus es?” “Dōnum tibi habeō!” “Nōnne mihi hoc iam dīxistī herī?” rogat Iūlia (exspectāns 'ita'). “Num putās mē herī mentītum esse?” respondet Mārcus (exspectāns 'minimē').

Notāvistīne: quis (pronōmen substantīvum), cūr (adverbium), nōnne (exspectāns respōnsum affirmātīvum), num (exspectāns respōnsum negātīvum)? Latīna, sīcut Anglica, distinguit quaestiōnēs 'sī/nōn' ā quaestiōnibus cum verbō interrogātīvō (WH-questions).

rules.heading: a) Quis, Quid: Pronomen Interrogativum
rules.body: Quis? (who? — personae) et quid? (what? — res) sunt fōrmae substantīvae. Dēclīnantur similiter prōnōminī relātīvō (quī, quae, quod — Gradus III), sed 'quis/quid' sunt fōrmae speciālēs nōminātīvī/accūsātīvī. Exemplum: Quis venit? ('Who comes?') Quid vidēs? ('What do you see?')

rules.heading: c) -ne, Num, Nonne
rules.body: Tria particulae fōrmant quaestiōnēs sī/nōn, cum implicātiōnibus dīversīs: -ne (suffīxum, neutrum, nūllam respōnsiōnem expectāns): Venīsne? ('Are you coming?') num (expectāns respōnsum negātīvum): Num venīs? ('You aren't coming, are you?') nōnne (expectāns respōnsum affirmātīvum): Nōnne venīs? ('You are coming, aren't you?')

examples: Quis est ille vir? — Who is that man?
Cūr flēs? — Why are you crying?
Ubi habitās? — Where do you live?
Quot fīliōs habēs? — How many sons do you have?
Nōnne hoc vidēs? — You see this, don't you?
Num crās veniēs? — You won't come tomorrow, will you?

commonMistakes.wrong: 'num' et '-ne' tractantur ut identici, sine differentia implicationis.
commonMistakes.right: '-ne' est neutrum; 'num' implicat responsum negativum exspectatum; 'nōnne' implicat responsum affirmativum exspectatum.
commonMistakes.why: Optio particulae communicat quid loquens iam credat esse verum, subtilitas perdita si omnes tractantur idem.

commonMistakes.wrong: 'Quis' adhibetur pro rebus (things), ut Anglicum 'what' informale ('who did you buy?').
commonMistakes.right: 'Quis' est pro personis ('who'); 'quid' est pro rebus ('what').
commonMistakes.why: Distinctio persona/res est stricta in Latina interrogativa, differenter ab usu colloquiali Anglico.

exercises.title: Donum Tibi Habeo!
exercises.passage: “Quis venit?” rogat Iūlia. “Ego,” dīcit Mārcus, rīdēns. “Cūr tam laetus es?” “Dōnum tibi habeō!” “Nōnne mihi hoc iam dīxistī herī?” rogat Iūlia. “Num putās mē herī mentītum esse?” respondet Mārcus. “Minimē — sed ubi est dōnum?” “Domī,” dīcit Mārcus. “Crās id feram.”
